title: Inversiya va urg‘u beruvchi tuzilmalar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida inkor ravishlardan keyin inversiya, what- va it-cleft gaplar hamda fronting yordamida fikringizga urg‘u berasiz va har bir tuzilmani mos uslubda (rasmiy, neytral, og‘zaki) ishlatasiz.

scenes.title: Inversiya va urg‘u beruvchi tuzilmalar
board: Lesson: Inversion and emphatic structures
(Inversiya va urg‘u beruvchi tuzilmalar)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda C1 yo‘l xaritasini chizdik va aniqlik, moslashuvchanlik hamda grammatik murakkablik C1 ning kalitlari ekanini ko‘rdik. Bugun shu murakkablikning eng yorqin vositalarini o‘rganamiz. Dars oxirida inkor ravishlardan keyin inversiya, cleft gaplar va fronting yordamida fikringizga urg‘u berasiz va ularni to‘g‘ri uslubda ishlatasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Today we look at how English adds emphasis through structure rather than volume: inversion, cleft sentences and fronting.
scenes.say_uz: Yana xush kelibsiz. Bugun ingliz tili ovoz balandligi emas, tuzilma orqali qanday urg‘u berishini ko‘ramiz: inversiya, cleft gaplar va fronting.

scenes.title: Ingliz va o‘zbek tilida urg‘u
board: Uzbek: word order + particles (-ku, -da, aynan)
English: fixed S–V–O order
→ special structures move the focus

examples.t: It was you that we needed.

scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida urg‘u berish oson: so‘z tartibini o‘zgartiramiz yoki “-ku”, “-da”, “aynan” kabi yuklamalarni qo‘shamiz. Fe’ldan oldingi so‘z odatda diqqat markazida bo‘ladi. Ingliz tilida esa so‘z tartibi qat’iy: ega, kesim, to‘ldiruvchi. Shuning uchun urg‘u uchun maxsus tuzilmalar bor. Ular gapni qayta quradi va kerakli qismni diqqat markaziga chiqaradi.
scenes.say: Uzbek can simply move words around or add a particle. English word order is far more rigid, so it relies on special structures to shift the focus.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbek tili so‘zlarni joyidan siljitadi yoki yuklama qo‘shadi. Ingliz tilida so‘z tartibi qat’iy, shuning uchun urg‘u maxsus tuzilmalar orqali beriladi.

scenes.title: Inversiya: asosiy qolip
board: Negative adverbial + AUXILIARY + SUBJECT + verb
I have never seen… → Never have I seen…
(xuddi so‘roq gapdagi tartib)

examples.t: Never have I seen such a mess.
Rarely does she complain.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi nuqta: inkor ravishlardan keyin inversiya. Agar “never”, “rarely”, “seldom” kabi inkor yoki cheklovchi so‘zni gap boshiga chiqarsak, yordamchi fe’l egadan oldin keladi, xuddi so‘roq gapdagidek. “I have never seen such a mess” o‘rniga “Never have I seen such a mess.” Ma’no o‘sha, lekin ohang ancha kuchli va dramatik.
scenes.say: Put a negative adverbial first, and the auxiliary comes before the subject, just as in a question. I have never seen becomes: never have I seen.
scenes.say_uz: Inkor ravishni boshga qo‘ysangiz, yordamchi fe’l egadan oldin keladi, xuddi so‘roqdagidek: never have I seen.

scenes.title: Yordamchi fe’l qayerdan?
board: has/had/will/can → move it: Seldom can we…
no auxiliary → add do/does/did: Rarely did he…
be → Seldom is it so quiet.

examples.t: Under no circumstances should you open this door.
examples.uz: Hech qanday holatda bu eshikni ochmasligingiz kerak.

examples.t: Seldom is the city so quiet.

scenes.say_native: Gapda yordamchi fe’l yoki modal bo‘lsa, o‘shani egadan oldinga chiqaramiz: “Seldom can we afford it.” Agar oddiy present yoki past simple bo‘lsa, so‘roqdagidek “do”, “does”, “did” qo‘shamiz: “He rarely smiled” bo‘ladi “Rarely did he smile.” “Be” fe’li esa o‘zi joy almashadi: “Seldom is the city so quiet.” Asosiy fe’l “did” dan keyin infinitiv shaklga qaytadi.
scenes.say: If there's an auxiliary or modal, move it. If there isn't, add do, does or did, as in a question: rarely did he smile. The verb be simply swaps places.
scenes.say_uz: Yordamchi yoki modal bo‘lsa, uni ko‘chiring. Bo‘lmasa, do, does yoki did qo‘shing: rarely did he smile. Be o‘zi joy almashadi.

scenes.title: Inkor ravishlar ro‘yxati
board: Never · Rarely · Seldom · Hardly ever
At no time · Under no circumstances · On no account
Nowhere · In no way · Little

examples.t: At no time was the public in danger.
examples.uz: Jamoat hech bir lahzada xavf ostida bo‘lmagan.

examples.t: Nowhere is this more obvious than in education.
examples.uz: Bu hech qayerda ta’limdagidek yaqqol ko‘rinmaydi.

scenes.say_native: Inversiyani chaqiradigan iboralar guruhlari. Chastota: “never”, “rarely”, “seldom”, “hardly ever”. Qat’iy taqiq: “under no circumstances”, “on no account”, “at no time”. Joy va usul: “nowhere”, “in no way”. Rasmiy hujjatlar va bayonotlarda ular juda ko‘p: “At no time was the public in danger.” E’tibor bering: “no” bilan boshlangan ibora butun gapni inkor qilishi kerak.
scenes.say: Common triggers: never, rarely, seldom, at no time, under no circumstances, on no account, nowhere and in no way. Official statements love them.
scenes.say_uz: Keng tarqalganlari: never, rarely, seldom, at no time, under no circumstances, on no account, nowhere, in no way. Rasmiy bayonotlarda ko‘p.

scenes.title: Hardly, No sooner, Scarcely
board: Hardly had I… when…
No sooner had I… than…
Scarcely had I… when…
(past perfect + past simple)

examples.t: No sooner had we sat down than the lights went out.
Hardly had she arrived when the phone rang.

scenes.say_native: Bir voqeadan keyin darhol ikkinchisi sodir bo‘lganini aytish uchun maxsus juftliklar bor. “No sooner had I… than…”, “Hardly had I… when…”, “Scarcely had I… when…”. Birinchi qismda past perfect va inversiya, ikkinchisida oddiy past simple. O‘zbekchada buni “-ishi bilan” deb aytamiz: “O‘tirishimiz bilan chiroq o‘chdi.” Juftliklarni almashtirib yubormang.
scenes.say: To say one thing happened immediately after another: no sooner had we sat down than the lights went out. Hardly and scarcely take when.
scenes.say_uz: Bir voqeadan darhol keyin ikkinchisi: no sooner had we sat down than the lights went out. Hardly va scarcely when bilan keladi.

scenes.title: Not only, Not until, Only
board: Not only did she win, but she also…
Not until I left did I realise…
Only when / Only after / Only then + inversion

examples.t: Not until the next morning did we learn the truth.
examples.uz: Faqat ertasi kuni ertalab haqiqatni bildik.

examples.t: Only then did I understand.

scenes.say_native: Yana uchta muhim guruh. “Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.” “Not until” va “only” bilan boshlangan ibora esa ko‘pincha ikki qismli: “Not until I left did I realise.” Diqqat: inversiya birinchi qismda emas, asosiy gapda bo‘ladi. “Only when I got home did I notice.” “Only then”, “only by”, “only after” ham xuddi shunday ishlaydi.
scenes.say: With not until and only when, the inversion comes in the main clause, not the time clause: only when I got home did I notice the damage.
scenes.say_uz: Not until va only when bilan inversiya vaqt qismida emas, asosiy gapda bo‘ladi: only when I got home did I notice.

scenes.title: Little va So/Such
board: Little did they know that…
So + adjective + be + subject + that…
Such + be + noun + that…

examples.t: Little did they know that the house was empty.
examples.uz: Ular uy bo‘sh ekanini xayollariga ham keltirmagan edi.

examples.t: So strong was the wind that trees fell.
examples.uz: Shamol shunchalik kuchli ediki, daraxtlar qulab tushdi.

scenes.say_native: “Little” bu yerda “ozgina” emas, “umuman” degan inkor ma’noni beradi: “Little did they know”, ular xayollariga ham keltirmagan edi. Hikoyalarda juda keng tarqalgan. Natija gaplarida ham inversiya bor: “So strong was the wind that trees fell.” “Such” bilan: “Such was the demand that tickets sold out in minutes.” Bu tuzilmalar adabiy va publitsistik uslubga xos.
scenes.say: Little did they know means they had no idea at all. For results: so strong was the wind that trees fell; such was the demand that tickets sold out.
scenes.say_uz: Little did they know ular umuman bilmaganini bildiradi. Natija uchun: so strong was the wind that…; such was the demand that…

scenes.title: Inversiyadagi xatolar
board: ✗ Never I have seen… → ✓ Never have I seen…
✗ No sooner had I arrived when… → ✓ …than…
✗ Rarely he goes out. → ✓ Rarely does he go out.
✗ Not until did I leave I realised → ✓ Not until I left did I realise
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta tipik xato. Birinchisi, ravishni boshga qo‘yib, inversiyani unutish: “Never I have seen”. Ikkinchisi, “no sooner” dan keyin “when”: to‘g‘risi “than”. Uchinchisi, “do” ni unutish: “Rarely he goes out” emas, “Rarely does he go out”, “goes” esa “go” ga qaytadi. To‘rtinchisi, inversiyani noto‘g‘ri qismga qo‘yish: “not until” bilan asosiy gap ag‘dariladi.
scenes.say: Don't forget to invert, don't forget do, use than after no sooner, and with not until, invert the main clause.
scenes.say_uz: Inversiyani va do ni unutmang, no sooner dan keyin than, not until da esa asosiy gapni ag‘daring.

scenes.title: Inversiya bilan qayta yozing
board: 1 I have rarely heard such nonsense. (Rarely…)
2 She didn't realise the danger until later. (Not until…)
3 As soon as he left, it started to rain. (No sooner…)
4 You must not tell anyone. (Under no circumstances…)
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gapni berilgan so‘z bilan boshlab, inversiya orqali qayta yozing. Har birida o‘zingizdan so‘rang: yordamchi fe’l bormi, yoki “do”, “did” kerakmi? Uchinchisida past perfect va to‘g‘ri juftlikni eslang. Javoblarni ovoz chiqarib, dramatik ohangda ayting.
scenes.say: Rewrite the four sentences starting with the words in brackets.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rt gapni qavsdagi so‘zlar bilan boshlab qayta yozing.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Rarely have I heard such nonsense.
2 Not until later did she realise the danger.
3 No sooner had he left than it started to rain.
4 Under no circumstances must you tell anyone.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “Rarely have I heard such nonsense”, “have” egadan oldinga o‘tdi. Ikkinchi: “Not until later did she realise the danger”, “didn’t” yo‘qoldi, “did” inversiyada. Uchinchi: “No sooner had he left than it started to rain.” To‘rtinchi: “Under no circumstances must you tell anyone”, “should” ham to‘g‘ri. “Not” endi kerak emas, inkor iboraning o‘zida.
scenes.say: Rarely have I heard such nonsense. Not until later did she realise the danger. No sooner had he left than it started to rain. Under no circumstances must you tell anyone.
scenes.say_uz: Rarely have I heard such nonsense. Not until later did she realise. No sooner had he left than it rained. Under no circumstances must you tell anyone.

scenes.title: Tinglang: rektor nutqi
board: Listen: a university head's speech
scenes.say_native: Birinchi tinglash matni: universitet rektorining bitiruvchilarga nutqi. Rasmiy, tantanali uslub. Unda nechta inversiya borligini sanang va har biri qaysi so‘z bilan boshlanganini eslab qoling. Nutq qaysi voqealar haqida ekaniga ham e’tibor bering, keyin uchta savol beraman.
scenes.say: Graduates, never have I been prouder of a class. Not only did you study through a pandemic, but you also volunteered in hospitals. Little did we know, four years ago, how much you would achieve. Only now do I fully understand your courage. And on no account should you forget where you came from.
scenes.say_uz: Bitiruvchilar, hech qachon biror kurs bilan bunchalik faxrlanmaganman. Siz pandemiya davrida nafaqat o‘qidingiz, balki kasalxonalarda ko‘ngilli ham bo‘ldingiz. To‘rt yil oldin qanchalik ko‘p narsaga erishishingizni xayolimizga ham keltirmagan edik. Faqat endi jasoratingizni to‘liq tushunaman. Va hech qachon qayerdan kelganingizni unutmang.

scenes.title: Tinglash savollari
board: 1 How many inversions did you hear?
2 What did the graduates do besides studying?
3 What must they never forget?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi, nechta inversiyani eshitdingiz va ular qaysi so‘zlar bilan boshlandi? Ikkinchi, bitiruvchilar o‘qishdan tashqari nima qilgan? Uchinchi, rektor ularni nimani unutmaslikka chaqirdi? Kerak bo‘lsa, nutqni qayta tinglang va har bir inversiyani yozib oling.
scenes.say: Answer the three questions on the board.
scenes.say_uz: Ekrandagi uchta savolga javob bering.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Five: Never have I · Not only did you · Little did we know · Only now do I · On no account should you
2 They volunteered in hospitals.
3 Where they came from
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: beshta inversiya bor: “never have I”, “not only did you”, “little did we know”, “only now do I” va “on no account should you”. Ikkinchi: ular kasalxonalarda ko‘ngilli bo‘lgan. Uchinchi: qayerdan kelganlarini unutmaslik. Ko‘ryapsizmi, rasmiy nutqda inversiya tinglovchini hayajonlantiradi va har bir fikrga og‘irlik beradi.
scenes.say: Five inversions. They volunteered in hospitals. And they must never forget where they came from.
scenes.say_uz: Beshta inversiya. Ular kasalxonalarda ko‘ngilli bo‘lgan. Qayerdan kelganlarini unutmasliklari kerak.

scenes.title: Cleft gaplar: g‘oya
board: cleft = bo‘lingan gap
Wh-cleft: What I need is a holiday.
It-cleft: It was Anna who called.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi nuqta: cleft gaplar. “Cleft” bo‘lingan degani: bitta oddiy gapni ikki qismga ajratib, bir qismini diqqat markaziga qo‘yamiz. Ikki asosiy turi bor. “What” bilan: “I need a holiday” o‘rniga “What I need is a holiday.” “It” bilan: “Anna called” o‘rniga “It was Anna who called.” Ikkalasi ham og‘zaki va yozma nutqda juda keng tarqalgan.
scenes.say: A cleft sentence splits one idea into two parts to highlight one of them. What I need is a holiday. It was Anna who called.
scenes.say_uz: Cleft gap bitta fikrni ikki qismga bo‘lib, birini ajratib ko‘rsatadi. What I need is a holiday. It was Anna who called.

scenes.title: What-cleft
board: What + clause + is/was + focus
What I need is time.
What I did was (to) call the police.
What happened was (that)…

examples.t: What annoys me is his attitude.
What we did was cancel the trip.
examples.uz: Biz qilgan narsa safarni bekor qilish bo‘ldi.

scenes.say_native: What-cleft qolipi: “What” va gapcha, keyin “is” yoki “was”, so‘ng urg‘u beriladigan qism. “What I need is time.” Agar harakatga urg‘u bermoqchi bo‘lsak, “do” ishlatamiz: “What I did was call the police”, ba’zan “to call”. Voqea uchun: “What happened was that the server crashed.” Bu tuzilma tinglovchida kutish hosil qiladi, muhim ma’lumot esa oxirida keladi.
scenes.say: What-clefts build suspense: the important information arrives at the end. What I need is time. To focus on an action, use do: what I did was call the police.
scenes.say_uz: What-cleft kutish hosil qiladi, muhim ma’lumot oxirida keladi. Harakatga urg‘u uchun do: what I did was call the police.

scenes.title: It-cleft
board: It is/was + focus + who/that + rest
It was Anna who called. (not Ben)
It's not the money that worries me.
It was in 2010 that we met.

examples.t: It was in Samarkand that they first met.
examples.uz: Ular aynan Samarqandda ilk bor tanishgan.

scenes.say_native: It-cleft qolipi: “It is” yoki “It was”, urg‘u beriladigan qism, keyin “who” yoki “that”. Odam uchun “who” yoki “that”, boshqa narsalar uchun “that”. Bu tuzilma ko‘pincha qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi: “It was Anna who called”, ya’ni Ben emas, Anna. Vaqt va joyga ham urg‘u berish mumkin: “It was in Samarkand that they first met.” Bu o‘zbekchadagi “aynan” ga juda yaqin.
scenes.say: It-clefts often correct or contrast: it was Anna who called, not Ben. You can also highlight a time or place: it was in Samarkand that they first met.
scenes.say_uz: It-cleft ko‘pincha tuzatish yoki qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi: Ben emas, Anna qo‘ng‘iroq qildi. Vaqt yoki joyga ham urg‘u berish mumkin.

scenes.title: Boshqa cleft shakllar
board: All I want is… (faqat)
The thing is… · The reason (why)… is that…
The place where… · The person who…
Reversed: A holiday is what I need.

examples.t: All I want is a quiet evening.
The reason I left is that I was bored.

scenes.say_native: What-cleft ning qarindoshlari ham bor. “All I want is a quiet evening”, ya’ni faqat shu. “The thing is…” og‘zaki nutqda muammoni kiritadi. “The reason I left is that…”. “The place where we met was a tiny café.” Teskari shakl ham mumkin: “A holiday is what I need.” O‘zbekchadagi “Menga kerak bo‘lgani — dam olish” tuzilmasi deyarli xuddi shunday.
scenes.say: Related patterns: all I want is, the thing is, the reason is that, the place where. You can also reverse it: a holiday is what I need.
scenes.say_uz: O‘xshash qoliplar: all I want is, the thing is, the reason is that, the place where. Teskarisi ham mumkin: a holiday is what I need.

scenes.title: Cleft gaplardagi xatolar
board: ✗ What I need it is time. → ✓ What I need is time.
✗ What I did was I called… → ✓ What I did was call…
✗ It was Anna which called. → ✓ who / that
✗ The reason is because… → ✓ The reason is that…
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta xato. Birinchisi, ortiqcha “it”: “What I need it is time”, bu o‘zbekchadagi “kerak bo‘lgani bu” tuzilmasidan keladi. Ikkinchisi, harakatni yana to‘liq gap qilib yozish: “What I did was I called”, to‘g‘risi “call”. Uchinchisi, odam uchun “which”. To‘rtinchisi, “the reason is because”: og‘zaki nutqda eshitiladi, lekin rasmiy yozuvda “the reason is that” deng.
scenes.say: No extra it: what I need is time. After what I did was, use the base verb. Use who for people. In formal writing, the reason is that, not because.
scenes.say_uz: Ortiqcha it yo‘q. What I did was dan keyin fe’lning asosiy shakli. Odam uchun who. Rasmiy yozuvda the reason is that.

scenes.title: Cleft gap tuzing
board: 1 I love the silence of the mountains. (What…)
2 Tom broke the window, not Sam. (It was…)
3 I only want some sleep. (All…)
4 She resigned. (What she did…)
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gapni cleft gapga aylantiring, qavsdagi boshlanishdan foydalaning. Ikkinchisida qarama-qarshilik bor, demak qaysi tur mos? To‘rtinchisida harakatga urg‘u beriladi, “do” qolipini eslang. Javoblarni ovoz chiqarib, urg‘uli so‘zni kuchliroq aytib ko‘ring.
scenes.say: Turn each sentence into a cleft sentence, using the words in brackets.
scenes.say_uz: Har gapni qavsdagi so‘zlar bilan cleft gapga aylantiring.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 What I love is the silence of the mountains.
2 It was Tom who/that broke the window.
3 All I want is some sleep.
4 What she did was resign.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “What I love is the silence of the mountains.” Ikkinchi: “It was Tom who broke the window”, “that” ham to‘g‘ri; qarama-qarshilik uchun it-cleft eng mos. Uchinchi: “All I want is some sleep”, “only” endi kerak emas, uning ma’nosi “all” da. To‘rtinchi: “What she did was resign”, fe’l asosiy shaklda.
scenes.say: What I love is the silence of the mountains. It was Tom who broke the window. All I want is some sleep. What she did was resign.
scenes.say_uz: What I love is the silence of the mountains. It was Tom who broke the window. All I want is some sleep. What she did was resign.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: urg‘u va bog‘lanish
board: It was ANNA who called. (tonic stress on focus)
What I NEED is TIME.
what_I → /wɒtaɪ/ · was → /wəz/
scenes.say_native: Cleft gapda asosiy urg‘u diqqat markazidagi so‘zga tushadi: “It was ANNA who called.” Qolgan qism, “it was” va “who called”, pastroq va tezroq aytiladi, “was” zaif shaklda “wəz”. What-cleft da ikkita cho‘qqi bo‘ladi: “What I NEED is TIME.” So‘zlar bog‘lanadi: “what I” deyarli bitta so‘zdek eshitiladi. Bu ohangsiz cleft gap o‘z kuchini yo‘qotadi.
scenes.say: Stress the focus and keep the rest light. It was Anna who called. What I need is time. Notice how what and I link together.
scenes.say_uz: Diqqat markazini urg‘u bilan, qolganini yengil ayting. It was Anna who called. What I need is time. What va I bog‘lanadi.

scenes.title: Fronting: nimani boshga chiqaramiz
board: Object: This I cannot accept.
Complement: Particularly worrying is the cost.
Place + full inversion: On the hill stood a castle.
Here comes the bus. / Here it comes.

examples.t: Into the room walked a stranger.

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi nuqta: fronting, ya’ni gapning bir qismini boshga chiqarish. To‘ldiruvchi: “This I cannot accept.” Sifat va kesimning ot qismi: “Particularly worrying is the cost.” Joy yoki harakat yo‘nalishi bilan to‘liq inversiya: “On the hill stood a castle”, “Into the room walked a stranger.” Bu yerda “do” qo‘shilmaydi, asosiy fe’lning o‘zi egadan oldin keladi.
scenes.say: Fronting moves a part of the sentence to the front. This I cannot accept. Particularly worrying is the cost. After place expressions, the whole verb comes first: on the hill stood a castle.
scenes.say_uz: Fronting gapning bir qismini boshga chiqaradi. Joy iboralaridan keyin butun fe’l egadan oldin keladi: on the hill stood a castle.

scenes.title: Yon berish fronting
board: Adjective + as/though + subject + verb
Strange as it may seem, …
Much as I admire him, …
Try as I might, …

examples.t: Much as I admire him, I can't agree.
examples.uz: Uni qanchalik hurmat qilsam ham, rozi bo‘lolmayman.

examples.t: Try as I might, I couldn't open it.

scenes.say_native: Yana bir chiroyli qolip: yon berish ma’nosida fronting. “Strange as it may seem”, qanchalik g‘alati tuyulmasin. “Tired though she was, she kept working.” “Much as I admire him, I can’t agree.” “Try as I might, I couldn’t open it.” O‘zbekchadagi “qanchalik… -sa ham” ga to‘g‘ri keladi. Bu “although” ga qaraganda ancha kuchli va adabiy eshitiladi.
scenes.say: For concession: strange as it may seem; tired though she was; much as I admire him; try as I might. They're stronger than although.
scenes.say_uz: Yon berish uchun: strange as it may seem; tired though she was; much as I admire him; try as I might. Bular although dan kuchliroq.

scenes.title: Fronting xatolari
board: ✗ Here comes it. → ✓ Here it comes.
✗ On the hill a castle stood. (weak, not wrong) → ✓ On the hill stood a castle.
✗ Strange as may it seem → ✓ Strange as it may seem
scenes.say_native: Uchta nozik joy. Birinchisi, olmosh bilan to‘liq inversiya bo‘lmaydi: “Here comes the bus”, lekin “Here it comes”, “Here comes it” emas. Ikkinchisi, joy iborasidan keyin inversiya qilmaslik xato emas, lekin ta’sirli emas. Uchinchisi, yon berish qolipida ega va fe’l odatiy tartibda qoladi: “Strange as it may seem”, “as may it seem” emas.
scenes.say: With a pronoun subject there's no inversion: here it comes, not here comes it. And in concession patterns the subject stays first: strange as it may seem.
scenes.say_uz: Olmosh bilan inversiya yo‘q: here it comes. Yon berish qolipida ega oldin: strange as it may seem.

scenes.title: Fronting bilan qayta yozing
board: 1 A tiny cottage stood at the end of the road. (At the end…)
2 Although it may sound odd, I enjoy exams. (Odd as…)
3 Although I tried hard, I couldn't remember. (Try as…)
scenes.say_native: Uchta gapni qavsdagi boshlanish bilan qayta yozing. Birinchisida joy iborasidan keyin to‘liq inversiya kerak. Ikkinchi va uchinchisida yon berish qolipi: “although” yo‘qoladi, ega va fe’l tartibiga e’tibor bering. Javoblarni ovoz chiqarib, adabiy ohangda ayting.
scenes.say: Rewrite the three sentences, starting with the words in brackets.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta gapni qavsdagi so‘zlar bilan boshlab qayta yozing.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 At the end of the road stood a tiny cottage.
2 Odd as it may sound, I enjoy exams.
3 Try as I might, I couldn't remember.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “At the end of the road stood a tiny cottage”, joy iborasi, keyin fe’l, keyin ega. Ikkinchi: “Odd as it may sound, I enjoy exams”, “although” yo‘qoldi, uning ma’nosini “as” beradi. Uchinchi: “Try as I might, I couldn’t remember.” Bu qotib qolgan ibora, “try” asosiy shaklda va “might” bilan keladi.
scenes.say: At the end of the road stood a tiny cottage. Odd as it may sound, I enjoy exams. Try as I might, I couldn't remember.
scenes.say_uz: Yo‘l oxirida kichkina kulba turardi. G‘alati eshitilsa ham, imtihonlarni yoqtiraman. Qancha urinmay, eslay olmadim.

scenes.title: Tinglang: do‘stlar suhbati
board: Listen: Malika and Josh talk about a new job
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi tinglash matni: norasmiy suhbat. Malika va Josh Malikaning yangi ishi haqida gaplashmoqda. Bu yerda inversiya deyarli yo‘q, lekin cleft gaplar va fronting ko‘p. Ularni topishga harakat qiling va Malikani nima bezovta qilayotganini aniqlang. Ohangdagi urg‘ularga ham quloq soling.
scenes.say: Josh: So, how's the new job? Malika: Well, the people I like. The work, not so much. Josh: Really? Malika: The thing is, I spend all day in meetings. What I actually want is to build things. Josh: So talk to your manager. Malika: It was my manager who suggested the meetings! Josh: Ah. Tricky. Malika: Yeah. All I need is one free afternoon a week.
scenes.say_uz: Josh: Xo‘sh, yangi ish qanday? Malika: Odamlari yoqadi. Ishning o‘zi unchalik emas. Josh: Rostdanmi? Malika: Gap shundaki, kun bo‘yi yig‘ilishlarda o‘tiraman. Aslida men xohlagan narsa — biror narsa yaratish. Josh: Unda rahbaringiz bilan gaplashing. Malika: Yig‘ilishlarni taklif qilgan aynan rahbarim-ku! Josh: Voy. Qiyin. Malika: Ha. Menga faqat haftada bitta bo‘sh tushdan keyin kerak.

scenes.title: Tinglash savollari
board: 1 What does Malika like and dislike?
2 Find three cleft sentences.
3 Find one example of fronting.
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi, Malikaga ishida nima yoqadi va nima yoqmaydi? Ikkinchi, suhbatdan uchta cleft gapni toping. Uchinchi, bitta fronting misolini toping, ya’ni to‘ldiruvchi gap boshiga chiqqan joyni. Iboralarni aynan matndagidek ayting, kerak bo‘lsa, suhbatni qayta tinglang.
scenes.say: Answer the three questions on the board.
scenes.say_uz: Ekrandagi uchta savolga javob bering.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Likes the people; dislikes endless meetings
2 The thing is… · What I actually want is… · It was my manager who… · All I need is…
3 The people I like.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: hamkasblar yoqadi, lekin kun bo‘yi yig‘ilishlar yoqmaydi. Ikkinchi: “What I actually want is to build things”, “It was my manager who suggested the meetings”, “All I need is one free afternoon”, “The thing is” ham shunga yaqin. Uchinchi: “The people I like”, to‘ldiruvchi boshga chiqqan, qarama-qarshilik uchun: odamlar yoqadi, ish esa yo‘q.
scenes.say: She likes the people but not the meetings. What I actually want is, it was my manager who, all I need is. And the fronted object: the people I like.
scenes.say_uz: Odamlar yoqadi, yig‘ilishlar yoqmaydi. What I actually want is, it was my manager who, all I need is. Fronting: the people I like.

scenes.title: Uslub: qaysi tuzilma qayerda
board: Inversion → formal: speeches, reports, literature
Clefts → everywhere, very common in speech
Fronting → stories, rhetoric; concession = formal
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi nuqta: uslub. Inkor ravishlardan keyin inversiya asosan rasmiy: nutqlar, hisobotlar, adabiyot, rasmiy ogohlantirishlar. Cleft gaplar esa hamma joyda, ayniqsa og‘zaki nutqda: “What I mean is…”, “The thing is…”. Joy iboralari bilan fronting hikoyalarga xos. Yon berish qolipi, “much as I admire him”, rasmiy va adabiy ohangga ega.
scenes.say: Inversion after negatives is mainly formal. Clefts are everywhere, especially in speech. Fronting after place expressions belongs to storytelling.
scenes.say_uz: Inkordan keyin inversiya asosan rasmiy. Cleft gaplar hamma joyda, ayniqsa og‘zaki nutqda. Joy iborasi bilan fronting hikoyalarga xos.

scenes.title: Bitta fikr, uch uslub
board: Formal: Under no circumstances should you leave.
Neutral: You mustn't leave under any circumstances.
Informal: No way are you leaving!

examples.t: No way am I doing that!

scenes.say_native: Bitta fikrni uch uslubda solishtiring. Rasmiy: “Under no circumstances should you leave.” Neytral: “You mustn’t leave under any circumstances.” Norasmiy: “No way are you leaving!” Ha, “no way” bilan og‘zaki inversiya ham bor, u juda jonli eshitiladi. “Little did I know” ham kundalik hikoyalarda qotib qolgan ibora sifatida ishlatiladi, ko‘pincha hazil ohangida.
scenes.say: Compare: under no circumstances should you leave; you mustn't leave under any circumstances; no way are you leaving! Colloquial inversion exists too.
scenes.say_uz: Solishtiring: rasmiy under no circumstances should you leave; neytral you mustn’t leave; norasmiy no way are you leaving!

scenes.title: Emphatic do va kuchaytiruvchilar
board: I DO understand. (rostdan)
She DID call — I checked.
nothing whatsoever · not at all · the very thing

examples.t: I do understand your concerns.
That's the very thing I wanted.

scenes.say_native: Yana bir neytral urg‘u vositasi: tasdiq gapda “do”, “does”, “did”. “I do understand your concerns”, ya’ni chindan tushunaman. Ko‘pincha e’tirozga javob sifatida: “She did call, I checked.” Inkorni kuchaytirish uchun “at all” va “whatsoever”: “nothing whatsoever”. “The very” esa “aynan” ma’nosini beradi: “the very thing I wanted”. Bular har qanday uslubda ishlaydi.
scenes.say: Emphatic do works in any register: I do understand your concerns. Strengthen negatives with at all or whatsoever, and use the very for exactly.
scenes.say_uz: Urg‘uli do har qanday uslubda ishlaydi: I do understand. Inkorni at all yoki whatsoever bilan kuchaytiring, the very aynan degani.

scenes.title: Uslub xatolari
board: ✗ Text to a friend: 'Seldom have I eaten such pizza.' (too formal)
✗ Essay with inversion in every sentence
✓ 1–2 inversions per essay, at key points
scenes.say_native: Uslub xatolari ikki xil. Birinchisi, rasmiy inversiyani norasmiy joyda ishlatish. Do‘stga xabarda “Seldom have I eaten such pizza” yozsangiz, bu kulgili yoki kinoyali eshitiladi. Ikkinchisi, ortiqcha ishlatish. Esseda har gapda inversiya bo‘lsa, matn sun’iy ko‘rinadi. Bitta-ikkita inversiya, eng muhim fikrda, masalan kirish yoki xulosada, eng yaxshi ta’sir beradi.
scenes.say: Use formal inversion in a casual message and it sounds ironic. Overuse it in an essay and it sounds artificial. One or two, at key moments, is enough.
scenes.say_uz: Norasmiy xabarda rasmiy inversiya kinoyali eshitiladi. Esseda ortiqcha bo‘lsa, sun’iy ko‘rinadi. Muhim joyda bitta-ikkitasi yetarli.

scenes.title: Uslubni tanlang
board: 1 A safety notice in a lab
2 A chat with a friend about a bad film
3 The conclusion of a formal report
a) What I hated was the ending. b) On no account should chemicals be removed. c) Not only did costs fall, but quality also improved.
scenes.say_native: Uchta vaziyat va uchta gap bor. Har bir vaziyatga eng mos gapni tanlang va nega mosligini bir jumla bilan tushuntiring. Qaysi tuzilma rasmiy, qaysi biri og‘zaki nutqqa yaqin ekanini eslang. Ogohlantirish, do‘stona suhbat va rasmiy hisobotning ohangi bir-biridan qanchalik farq qilishini o‘ylab ko‘ring.
scenes.say: Match each situation to the most suitable sentence.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir vaziyatni eng mos gap bilan moslang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 → b (formal prohibition)
2 → a (cleft, conversational)
3 → c (formal, emphatic summary)
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Laboratoriya ogohlantirishi “b”: “On no account should chemicals be removed”, rasmiy taqiq va majhul nisbat. Do‘st bilan suhbat “a”: “What I hated was the ending”, cleft gap, tabiiy og‘zaki uslub. Rasmiy hisobot xulosasi “c”: “Not only did costs fall, but quality also improved”, ikki natijani kuchli bog‘laydi.
scenes.say: The lab notice is b, the chat is a, and the report conclusion is c.
scenes.say_uz: Laboratoriya — b, suhbat — a, hisobot xulosasi — c.

scenes.title: Aralash mashq: urg‘u bering
board: 1 I didn't know how serious it was. (Little…)
2 The noise drives me mad. (What…)
3 You can succeed only by working hard. (Only by…)
4 I admire her, but I think she's wrong. (Much as…)
scenes.say_native: Endi hamma tuzilmalarni aralashtiramiz. To‘rtta gapni qavsdagi boshlanish bilan qayta yozing. Har birida qaysi tuzilma ishlatilayotganini o‘zingizga ayting: inversiya, cleft yoki fronting. Uy vazifasi ham xuddi shunday bo‘ladi, shuning uchun bu yaxshi mashq.
scenes.say: Rewrite each sentence for emphasis, starting with the words in brackets.
scenes.say_uz: Har gapni qavsdagi so‘zlar bilan boshlab, urg‘u bilan qayta yozing.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Little did I know how serious it was.
2 What drives me mad is the noise.
3 Only by working hard can you succeed.
4 Much as I admire her, I think she's wrong.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “Little did I know how serious it was”, inversiya, “didn’t” o‘rniga “did”. Ikkinchi: “What drives me mad is the noise”, cleft. Uchinchi: “Only by working hard can you succeed”, “can” egadan oldinga o‘tdi. To‘rtinchi: “Much as I admire her, I think she’s wrong”, yon berish fronting, “but” endi kerak emas.
scenes.say: Little did I know how serious it was. What drives me mad is the noise. Only by working hard can you succeed. Much as I admire her, I think she's wrong.
scenes.say_uz: Little did I know. What drives me mad is the noise. Only by working hard can you succeed. Much as I admire her, she’s wrong.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: bir daqiqalik fikr
board: Topic: Is social media good for young people?
Use: 1 inversion · 1 cleft · 1 fronting
Formal or neutral register
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy vazifa. Mavzu: ijtimoiy tarmoqlar yoshlar uchun foydalimi? Bir daqiqa davomida fikringizni ayting. Kamida bitta inversiya, bitta cleft gap va bitta fronting ishlating. Uslub rasmiy yoki neytral bo‘lsin, xuddi munozara yoki imtihondagidek. Taymerni qo‘yib, ovoz chiqarib gapiring.
scenes.say: Speak for one minute on the topic, using one inversion, one cleft and one fronting.
scenes.say_uz: Mavzu bo‘yicha bir daqiqa gapiring: bitta inversiya, bitta cleft va bitta fronting bilan.

scenes.title: Namuna javob
board: Much as I enjoy… (fronting)
What worries me is… (cleft)
Rarely do… / Only when… (inversion)
scenes.say_native: Namunaga e’tibor bering: yon berish fronting bilan boshlanadi, cleft gap asosiy xavotirni ajratib ko‘rsatadi, inversiya esa xulosaga og‘irlik beradi. Har tuzilma faqat bir marta, eng kerakli joyda. Shunday muvozanat C1 darajadagi tabiiy nutqning belgisi.
scenes.say: Much as I enjoy social media myself, I think it does real harm to teenagers. What worries me most is the constant comparison with others. Rarely do young people see the reality behind those perfect photos. Only when schools teach media literacy will this begin to change.
scenes.say_uz: Ijtimoiy tarmoqlarni o‘zim yoqtirsam ham, ular o‘smirlarga jiddiy zarar yetkazadi deb o‘ylayman. Meni eng ko‘p tashvishlantiradigani boshqalar bilan doimiy solishtirish. Yoshlar o‘sha mukammal suratlar ortidagi haqiqatni kamdan-kam ko‘radi. Faqat maktablar media savodxonligini o‘rgatgandagina bu o‘zgara boshlaydi.

scenes.title: Xulosa
board: Negative adverbial + aux + subject: Never have I…
Clefts: What I need is… · It was … who…
Fronting: On the hill stood… · Much as I…
Register: inversion = formal · clefts = everywhere
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Inversiya: inkor yoki cheklovchi ibora boshda bo‘lsa, yordamchi fe’l egadan oldin keladi, kerak bo‘lsa “do” qo‘shiladi; “no sooner… than”, “not until” da esa asosiy gap ag‘dariladi. Cleft: “What I need is”, “It was… who”, “All I want is”. Fronting: joy iboralari va yon berish qolipi. Uslub: inversiya rasmiy, cleft hamma joyda, me’yor muhim.
scenes.say: Inversion after negatives, cleft sentences, fronting, and choosing the right register: four tools for adding emphasis with precision.
scenes.say_uz: Inkordan keyin inversiya, cleft gaplar, fronting va to‘g‘ri uslub: aniq urg‘u berishning to‘rt vositasi.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: rewrite 8 sentences with emphasis
At least 3 inversions · 3 clefts · 2 frontings
Label each one: formal or neutral
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: o‘zingiz yozgan yoki darslikdagi sakkizta oddiy gapni urg‘u bilan qayta yozing. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida uchta inversiya, uchta cleft gap va ikkita fronting bo‘lsin, yordamchi fe’l va “do” to‘g‘ri ishlatilsin, har bir gap yoniga rasmiy yoki neytral ekanini yozing. Keyingi darsda akademik lug‘atning eng muhim uch yuz so‘zini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Rewrite eight sentences with emphasis, using inversion, clefts and fronting, and label each one's register. Until next time!
scenes.say_uz: Sakkizta gapni inversiya, cleft va fronting bilan qayta yozing va har birining uslubini belgilang. Keyingi safargacha!

homework_uz: Sakkizta oddiy gapni urg‘u bilan qayta yozing: kamida uchta inversiya (never, not until, only when va boshqalar), uchta cleft gap va ikkita fronting. Mezon: yordamchi fe’l va do to‘g‘ri ishlatilgan, ma’no o‘zgarmagan va har bir gap yonida uslubi (rasmiy yoki neytral) ko‘rsatilgan.

options: Never I have seen such a view.
Never have I seen such a view.
Never I saw such a view.
Never seen I have such a view.
quiz.why_uz: Inkor ravishdan keyin yordamchi fe’l egadan oldin keladi.
Yordamchi fe’l yo‘q bo‘lsa, does qo‘shiladi, fe’l asosiy shaklda.

quiz.q: No sooner had we arrived ___ it started to snow.
quiz.why_uz: No sooner… than; hardly va scarcely esa when bilan.

options: Not until I left did I realise my mistake.
Not until did I leave I realised my mistake.
Not until I left I realised my mistake.
Not until I did leave I realised my mistake.
quiz.why_uz: Not until bilan inversiya asosiy gapda bo‘ladi.
Little bu yerda to‘liq inkor ma’nosini beradi.

options: What I need it is a break.
What I need is a break.
That I need is a break.
What I need, it a break.

quiz.why_uz: What … did was dan keyin fe’lning asosiy shakli keladi.

quiz.q: It was my brother ___ found the keys.

quiz.why_uz: Olmosh bilan to‘liq inversiya bo‘lmaydi: here it comes.

quiz.q: Which sentence is most suitable for a casual text to a friend?
options: Under no circumstances shall I attend.
Seldom have I been so bored.
What I really need is a nap.
At no time was I informed.
quiz.why_uz: Cleft gaplar og‘zaki va norasmiy nutqda tabiiy; inkor inversiya rasmiy.
